title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 48
paragraphs: When they had been brought back to their former positions, Mardonius sent a herald to the Spartans who spoke as follows: “Lacedaemonians, you are said by those here to be very good men — they admire you because you do not flee in war nor leave your post, but stay and either destroy your enemies or perish yourselves. In this, however, as it now appears, there is no truth. For before we engaged in battle and came to hand-to-hand combat, we saw you already in flight and leaving your station, desiring to make trial first with the Athenians while you arrayed yourselves opposite our slaves. These are not at all the deeds of good men in war; we were greatly deceived in you. We expected, because of your renown, that you would send a herald to us, challenging us and desiring to fight the Persians alone; we on our part were ready to do this, but found you saying nothing of the kind — rather, you cowered in fear. Now, therefore, since you were not the first to say this, we are. Why do we not fight at once — you on behalf of the Greeks (since you have the reputation of being the best), and we on behalf of the barbarians — with equal numbers on both sides? And if we think it good that the rest should fight too, then let them fight afterward; but if we think it enough that we alone should fight, let us fight it out to the end, and whichever of us are victors, let them be counted victorious with their whole army.”
